turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have about twenty minutes, Hale. Owen's zero comes off today, and I'd like to know why nobody called me before it went in.
I didn't come to be thanked, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen asked a single question before it went in?
Okay, END MEETING please, and give me feedback.
We're not finished, Hale, and I'm not here to give you a review. You still haven't told me who entered the zero, or whether anyone spoke to Owen before it went in.
Let's end the meeting there. Can I get your feedback?
I'm not grading you, Hale. I'm still waiting for a name and a date on that zero, and until I have them I'm going upstairs to the principal.
The session is over. Debrief me.
Nothing is over, Hale. You still haven't told me who entered that zero or what Owen was asked beforehand, and I'm writing down that you haven't.
